steps.name: Normalize counts and build expression matrix
caveats: VST on n=12 with one low-depth sample can still leave residual mean-variance dependence for that sample; flag rather than hide this in QC output
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon; small dataset (12000 x 12). One sample is a known low-depth outlier per the data profile caveat; normalization must be library-size aware (VST or size-factor-based) so this sample's score is not spuriously depressed by depth alone.
steps.question: Given the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, colon, UC-inflamed vs control) and the note that sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, what is a normalized, log-scale expression matrix suitable for single-sample gene-set scoring?
constraints: Do not remove sample_01 from the dataset — report its behavior, do not exclude it without explicit instruction
Use gene symbols (already present as row identifiers) with no additional ID mapping needed since hallmark gene sets use HGNC symbols
acceptance_criteria: Reads counts.csv (12000 x 13, first column gene symbol) and metadata.csv (12 x 2) and confirms sample columns match metadata rows
Applies DESeq2 variance-stabilizing transformation (or equivalent library-size-aware normalization) to the raw integer counts, producing a genes x samples normalized matrix
Explicitly reports sample_01's post-normalization library size / outlier status rather than silently dropping or ignoring it
Collapses/deduplicates any repeated gene symbols to unique rows (e.g. by max mean expression) before writing the matrix, since GSVA requires unique gene identifiers as rownames
Output normalized matrix (genes x 12 samples) and sample metadata are saved for downstream steps

steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway activity scoring per sample
caveats: With n=12 and 12000 background genes, some of the 50 hallmark sets may have low gene overlap after symbol matching — report overlap counts so downstream interpretation for sparsely-matched sets is appropriately cautious
steps.context: Reference: the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC gene symbols, GMT format) staged in the environment under the pathways category — use this file directly rather than any external download. GSVA is the appropriate method for a per-sample, unsupervised (condition-agnostic) pathway activity score from bulk RNA-seq.
steps.question: What is the per-sample GSVA activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, across the 12 colon samples (6 UC-inflamed, 6 control)?
constraints: Must use the human (not mouse/rat) Hallmark GMT since the dataset is Homo sapiens colon tissue
GSVA must be run condition-blind (do not pass condition labels into the scoring step itself) so scores are a per-sample property, not derived from the group comparison
acceptance_criteria: Loads the normalized expression matrix from T1S1 and the 50 MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (HGNC symbols) staged in the environment
Runs GSVA (kcdf appropriate for continuous/log-normalized data, e.g. Gaussian) producing a pathways x samples score matrix (50 hallmark sets x 12 samples)
Confirms gene symbol overlap between the expression matrix and each hallmark set is non-trivial (reports the number of matched genes per set) before scoring
Writes the full per-sample x per-pathway GSVA score matrix as a CSV — this is the 'pathway activity score for every sample' deliverable
Reports how sample_01 (the low-depth outlier) scores relative to its condition group, without excluding it

steps.name: Differential hallmark pathway activity: UC-inflamed vs control
caveats: With only 6 samples per group, statistical power is limited; borderline (unadjusted) findings should be reported as such, not elevated to firm conclusions
steps.context: Design: 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch — a standard two-group comparison on the GSVA score matrix produced in T1S2. This directly answers which pathways separate treated from control, complementing the heatmap's visual read.
steps.question: Which of the 50 hallmark pathways' GSVA activity scores differ significantly between the 6 UC-inflamed and 6 control colon samples?
constraints: Test only on the condition variable available in metadata.csv (inflamed vs control) — no additional covariates are documented in the data profile
State the small-n caveat (6 vs 6) plainly rather than overstating significance
acceptance_criteria: Runs an unpaired two-group test (moderated t-test via limma, or Welch's t-test with multiple-testing correction) comparing GSVA scores between the inflamed and control groups for each of the 50 hallmark pathways
Reports effect size (mean difference / log-fold-style delta in GSVA score), p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per pathway
Ranks and lists pathways passing adjusted p < 0.05 (or states clearly if none pass, given n=6 vs 6 unpaired power constraints)
Explicitly notes sample_01's leverage on its group's mean/variance in the low-depth outlier context flagged in T1S1

steps.name: Heatmap of hallmark pathway activity across samples
caveats: Unsupervised clustering of only 12 samples on 50 features can be visually dominated by one or two high-variance pathways; do not over-interpret dendrogram topology as a robust finding beyond what T1S3's statistics support
steps.context: Final deliverable requested by the research question: a heatmap of hallmark activity across all 12 samples with condition structure visible, built directly from the GSVA score matrix and informed by the differential-activity ranking.
steps.question: What does a heatmap of the 50 hallmark GSVA activity scores across all 12 colon samples show, and does it visually separate UC-inflamed from control samples?
constraints: Use the full 50 x 12 hallmark score matrix as the primary heatmap; do not subset to only significant pathways without also stating that a full-set version was produced
Condition annotation labels must use the actual metadata condition values (UC-inflamed / control), not generic 'group A/B' labels
acceptance_criteria: Produces a clustered heatmap (genes/pathways as rows, samples as columns or vice versa) of the GSVA score matrix from T1S2, with a top or side annotation bar for condition (UC-inflamed vs control)
Row (pathway) z-scoring or centering is applied for visualization contrast, while the underlying saved score matrix from T1S2 remains the un-scaled per-sample scores
Highlights (e.g. via ordering, annotation, or an accompanying pathway list) the top pathways from T1S3's differential test so the figure connects visually to the statistical result
Annotates sample_01 distinctly in the sample-side annotation given its known library-size caveat, so any visual outlier behavior is attributable rather than mysterious
Saves the heatmap as a static image file (PNG/PDF) and the ordered pathway/sample matrix used to build it

plan.title: UC colon RNA-seq: GSVA hallmark pathway activity heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol) with 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control colon samples, unpaired, single batch. Sample_01 has a library size ~4x below median, so it needs normalization that is robust to that outlier (VST/CPM, not raw counts) before any sample-level scoring. The research question asks for two related deliverables: (1) a per-sample pathway activity score, and (2) a heatmap of hallmark pathway activity across samples highlighting what separates treated (inflamed) from control. This is a single-sample gene-set scoring (GSVA) task on normalized expression, not a differential-expression-first workflow, so the plan goes: normalize counts -> GSVA against the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets (staged locally, 50 sets, HGNC symbols matching the gene-symbol row names in counts.csv) -> per-sample score matrix -> heatmap with condition annotation -> a light statistical step testing which hallmark pathways' GSVA scores differ significantly between inflamed and control (unpaired t-test/limma on the score matrix), which directly answers 'which pathways separate treated from control'. All steps operate on this specific 12-sample, 12000-gene colon dataset; no external cohort or public GEO data is required since the counts and metadata are already in hand.
